=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer-Side Review of the Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

## Key points

1. **Process.** The Seller says its positions were "settled at principal level", are "FINAL" and are "not intended to be re-opened." We should not accept that framing. These are the counterparty's assertions in its own draft, and I have no record of any such agreement. Before the mark-up goes out, please confirm with Wattlebridge principals whether anything was actually agreed. Until then, treat every point as open. The "market context" preamble is also advocacy, not neutral guidance. Some figures are within normal ranges, but the package as a whole is not "market".

2. **The Seller contradicts itself.** The Update says Bluefen is "addressed", Riverlark will be released, and the incident is "not expected to be material". The Seller's own Disclosure Letter says no Bluefen consent has been obtained, Riverlark is unpaid with security undischarged, and the incident investigation is still preliminary. We should use that inconsistency in the negotiation.

3. **The real risk is how the clauses combine.** Each limitation might be defensible alone. Together they work like this:
   - general disclosure of the entire data room and public records;
   - plus a constructive buyer-knowledge bar;
   - plus caps and time limits applying to *all* Claims;
   - plus non-reliance and exclusive remedy across the board.

   The result is that almost every known risk (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, DD-006, the bonuses) becomes unrecoverable. The warranties would be largely illusory. Our priority is breaking this structure, not haggling over percentages.

---

## Issue-by-issue analysis

### A. Limitation regime

**1. Cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m), applied to all Claims (cl 12.1, 12.8)**
- A 20% cap on *general* warranty claims is within a negotiable range. Applying it to "all Claims of any nature" is not.
- **Push back:** the 20% cap should cover general warranties only. Carve out the following, with a cap of 100% of the price (AUD 24m) or uncapped:
  - title, capacity and other fundamental warranties;
  - the tax indemnity and tax warranties;
  - all specific indemnities;
  - leakage and debt-free/cash-free adjustments;
  - fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment (uncapped).
- Consider an intermediate cap (for example 50% or more) for IP and data/privacy warranties. For a SaaS target these are core value drivers.

**2. De minimis of AUD 25,000 and basket of AUD 250,000, deductible (cl 12.2)**
- The basket is about 1.04% of price, and the de minimis about 0.1%. The bigger issue is that the basket is a **deductible**: only the excess above AUD 250k is recoverable. That permanently writes off the first AUD 250k of loss.
- **Push back:**
  - make it a **tipping basket** (first-dollar recovery once the threshold is crossed);
  - reduce the de minimis to around AUD 10k;
  - require that claims arising from the same or related facts aggregate for de minimis purposes;
  - exclude indemnity, tax, fundamental and fraud claims from both thresholds.
- The aggregation point matters here. The three "related" Sandbar renewals of AUD 110k each, and any multi-part DD-006 losses, show how fragmented claims could otherwise fall through.

**3. Time limits of 18 months, applied to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (cl 12.3/13)**
- 18 months for general warranties is acceptable, preferably with at least one full audit cycle after Completion.
- A blanket default to all Claims is not acceptable. **Push for:**
  - title and capacity: at least 6–7 years, aligned with the NSW *Limitation Act 1969* contract period;
  - tax: until 60 days after the ATO amendment period expires for the relevant year (generally 4 years, unlimited for fraud or evasion);
  - specific indemnities: matter-specific periods, for example DD-006 at least 3 years given regulatory and representative-claim risk;
  - fraud: no limit.
- Flip the default so that limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims unless expressly extended.

**4. Fundamental warranties subject to the same cap and time limits.** Reject. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. A title or capacity defect means we did not get what we paid AUD 24m for. These warranties must be capped at the full price and survive for the long period above.

**5. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to all Claims (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)**
- **Push back:** carve out fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller or its officers and advisers. Indemnities and tax claims should sit outside the general limitations schedule.
- Note that a non-reliance clause will not wholly exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under s 18 of the Australian Consumer Law. It can still affect causation and reliance arguments, so we should not concede it in broad form.

### B. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

**6. General disclosure of the data room and public records (Disclosure Letter 1.1–1.2)**
- Reject. A whole-data-room disclosure qualifies every warranty with everything in the data room, whether or not its significance is apparent.
- **Push for:**
  - only **fair, specific disclosure** against identified warranties, with enough detail for a buyer to assess nature and scope;
  - no general disclosure of the data room, Accounts or public registers. At most, allow named public searches conducted on a specified date.
- **Cut-off date:** the data room snapshot is 22 September 2026, about six weeks ago. Any later developments are not disclosed. Require warranties to be repeated at Completion with no Seller right to update disclosure to cure breaches. Any updated disclosure should give the Buyer a termination or claim right.
- Disclosure must expressly **not** qualify the tax indemnity, the specific indemnities, or the fundamental warranties.
- Para 1.4 (no admission) can stay. Para 11 helpfully confirms that the Seller is not advancing any agreed conclusion.

**7. Buyer knowledge bar (cl 8.3)**
- This is the single most damaging clause in the package. It covers the knowledge of the Buyer **and its advisers**, including anything **"discoverable"** from the data room or public records. That is a constructive-knowledge test, and it would bar claims for every disclosed issue, including the very matters we need indemnities for.
- **Push for:** deletion, with an express pro-sandbagging clause stating that the Buyer's rights are unaffected by any investigation or knowledge. At absolute fallback, limit it to the *actual* knowledge of a short list of named Wattlebridge individuals. Exclude advisers' knowledge, and never let it apply to indemnities, tax or fundamental warranties.
- **W&I interaction:** if we intend to use warranty and indemnity insurance, known matters such as Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 will be excluded from cover. That makes Seller-backed specific indemnities, and ideally an escrow, essential. Please confirm whether W&I is in scope.

### C. Specific deal risks

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3): about AUD 3.6m revenue, roughly 30% of FY26**
- The Seller says this is "addressed". Its own disclosure says there is no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- The Seller's proposal is weak on three counts:
  - "reasonable endeavours" is a soft obligation;
  - deeming the condition satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent means a consent with onerous or adverse conditions would still count;
  - the 11.3 conditions are left unaddressed.
- **Push for:**
  - a condition precedent requiring an **unconditional** written Bluefen consent, or one on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, with evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied;
  - the condition to be **waivable only by the Buyer**;
  - "all reasonable endeavours" by the Seller, Buyer involvement in communications with Bluefen, and a long-stop date with a Buyer walk right;
  - as fallback, a price adjustment, escrow or earn-out linked to Bluefen retention, plus a specific indemnity for loss of the contract caused by change of control.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7): about AUD 3.2m outstanding**
- A release "following Completion" is inconsistent with the agreed debt-free/cash-free basis. The change-of-control clause (8.1) is likely to be triggered at Completion, so the Company could be in default the moment we own it, with security still in place over its assets.
- **Push for:**
  - a payout letter from Riverlark before Completion confirming the exact payout figure, including per-diem interest and break costs;
  - a deed of release delivered **at** Completion, with PPSR and any other security discharges lodged or delivered in escrow;
  - repayment directly from the purchase price through the funds flow;
  - the facility, interest and break costs treated as Debt in the price mechanism.
- **Title risk:** check whether Riverlark's security extends to the **shares** held by Harbourglass, for example through a share mortgage or an all-assets security agreement given by the Seller. If it does, the release must also cover the shares.

**10. DD-005 Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 excluded from the funds flow**
- These bonuses are triggered by the sale. They will fall on the Company, and therefore on us, after Completion. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow pushes the cost onto us economically.
- On-costs are not addressed. Depending on the facts, these may include PAYG withholding, superannuation guarantee (12% from 1 July 2025, if the bonus counts as ordinary time earnings), NSW payroll tax (5.45%, subject to grouping and threshold), and workers compensation. Indicatively, total cost could be around AUD 490k or more, subject to tax advice.
- **Push for:**
  - the bonuses and all on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses or Debt and deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller;
  - payment through Company payroll at Completion, funded from the purchase price;
  - a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket covering any shortfall, including amounts linked to the continued-employment conditions that crystallise later;
  - a warranty that no other change-of-control or retention payments exist.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): AUD 180k open on SOW3**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP embedded in its product. The payment amount is secondary.
- The Seller's indemnity is "limited to the specific SOW3 payment", which addresses the payment but not the ownership risk. DD-010 is not bank verification, and the amount outstanding may be more than AUD 180k.
- **Push for:**
  - a completion deliverable or condition precedent: evidence of payment in full of all SOW3 fees, plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 Project Materials, with moral rights consents if relevant;
  - a broadened indemnity covering all loss from any failure of the Company to own or be free to use SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, injunctions, re-development and replacement costs;
  - that indemnity sitting outside the cap and basket and unaffected by disclosure or knowledge, with a survival period of at least 4–6 years;
  - an escrow or retention if the assignment is not delivered before Completion.

**12. DD-006 data export and possible privacy incident**
- About 1,240 records were potentially exposed (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September the investigation was preliminary, with no conclusion on access, scope or notification. "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's characterisation, not a disclosed fact.
- **Regulatory timing:** under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete a reasonable assessment within 30 days (s 26WH). Depending on when the incident was discovered, that window may already have passed. Since the December 2024 amendments, exposure also includes higher OAIC penalty tiers, infringement notices, and the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy (in force from June 2025).
- **Push for:**
  - an updated investigation or forensic report, with the Buyer given access before signing or Completion;
  - a documented NDB assessment and decision, with notification made if required;
  - a specific indemnity covering regulatory penalties to the extent legally indemnifiable, investigation and remediation costs, notification costs, and third-party or representative claims;
  - that indemnity outside the cap, basket and knowledge bar, with a survival period of at least 3 years;
  - a retention or escrow;
  - privacy and cyber warranties repeated at Completion;
  - interim covenants requiring the Seller to keep the Buyer informed and not to make regulatory communications without Buyer consultation.

**13. Sandbar renewals: 3 × AUD 110k (AUD 330k aggregate)**
- The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs". Its own disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. DD-008 and DD-011 are to be "read together", which suggests a linked commitment split into three parts.
- "Related" is ambiguous. If the supplier is a **related party** of Harbourglass, this could be **leakage**. Clarify which it is.
- **Push for:**
  - confirmation of when the renewals were entered into, and whether they breach interim conduct-of-business covenants;
  - their terms and any termination rights;
  - treatment as Debt or a working-capital liability if committed and unaccrued;
  - if related-party, treatment as leakage with dollar-for-dollar recovery;
  - aggregation of related claims, since each renewal individually exceeds the de minimis but the total falls within the AUD 250k basket.

**14. Tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime"**
- Reject. Tax should be covered by a stand-alone **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion periods:
  - dollar-for-dollar recovery;
  - no de minimis or basket;
  - capped at 100% of price;
  - aligned to ATO amendment periods;
  - with conduct-of-claims provisions.
- This should specifically cover payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses.
- IP warranties should carry an enhanced cap and time limit (see point 1).

**15. Title (DD-012)**
- A share register prepared by the Company is evidence, not proof. The Seller itself notes that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Push for:**
  - reconciliation of the register with ASIC records;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, which also addresses the Riverlark point above;
  - share certificates or a lost-certificate indemnity, executed transfers, and a no-encumbrance confirmation;
  - title and capacity as fundamental warranties (see point 4).

**16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The Seller gives its reading: notification only, and no consent triggered by a share sale. We should check both documents ourselves for change-of-control clauses or deemed-assignment provisions, since these are common in NSW leases.
- **Push for:** a warranty that no third-party consent is required for the transaction beyond those listed, and notifications delivered at or before Completion as a completion deliverable.

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Process framing | "FINAL, not to be re-opened" | Not accepted; confirm with principals; all points open |
| 2 | Cap | 20% applies to all Claims | 20% for general warranties only; 100% or uncapped for fundamental, tax, indemnities, leakage and fraud |
| 3 | Thresholds | AUD 25k de minimis, AUD 250k deductible basket | Tipping basket, about AUD 10k de minimis, aggregation of related claims, no thresholds for indemnities or tax |
| 4 | Time limits | 18 months for all Claims | 18 months general; 6–7 years title; ATO period plus 60 days for tax; matter-specific periods for indemnities |
| 5 | Fundamental warranties | Same as general | Full price cap, long survival |
| 6 | Non-reliance and exclusive remedy | All Claims | Carve out fraud and wilful concealment; indemnities and tax outside |
| 7 | Disclosure | Whole data room and public records | Specific, fair disclosure only; no qualification of indemnities, tax or fundamentals; repetition at Completion without cure |
| 8 | Buyer knowledge | Constructive, including advisers and "discoverable" | Delete and add pro-sandbagging clause; fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals only |
| 9 | Bluefen (30% of revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent counts | CP for unconditional consent plus cl 11.3 conditions met; Buyer-only waiver; long-stop date and walk right; fallback escrow or price protection |
| 10 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | Payout letter, release and PPSR discharges at Completion, paid from price as Debt; check any security over shares |
| 11 | DD-005 bonuses (AUD 420k plus on-costs) | Outside funds flow | Transaction Expense deducted from price, paid through payroll at Completion; specific indemnity |
| 12 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment | Proof of payment plus confirmatory assignment as CP or deliverable; full IP indemnity outside limits; escrow |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Updated forensic report, NDB assessment, specific indemnity outside limits, escrow, interim covenants |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Diligence the terms and dates; treat as Debt or leakage if applicable; aggregation |
| 15 | Tax and IP | General regime | Stand-alone tax indemnity; enhanced IP cap and period |
| 16 | Title | Share register only | ASIC and PPSR checks, completion deliverables, fundamental warranty |
| 17 | Lease and Mossvale | No consent needed (Seller's reading) | Verify independently; no-consents warranty; notices as completion deliverables |

**Suggested priorities for the mark-up:**
1. Remove the general disclosure, the constructive knowledge bar, and the "all Claims" reach of the limitations.
2. Secure Riverlark discharge and bonus treatment within the price mechanics.
3. Make Bluefen a robust condition precedent.
4. Obtain specific indemnities, with escrow, for Ironquay and DD-006.
5. Establish the tax indemnity and fundamental warranty carve-outs.

The headline cap and basket numbers are the most tradeable items if we need to give ground.

**Open items for the deal team:**
- whether W&I insurance is being pursued;
- the discovery date of the DD-006 incident;
- whether the Sandbar supplier is a related party of Harbourglass;
- the scope of Riverlark's security;
- tax adviser input on bonus on-costs.

I recommend we verify DD-007 and DD-009 directly rather than relying on the Seller's characterisation.

- **W&I interaction:** if we intend to use warranty and indemnity insurance, known matters such as Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay and DD-006 will be excluded from cover. That makes Seller-backed specific indemnities, and ideally an escrow, essential. Please confirm whether W&I is in scope.

### C. Specific deal risks

**8. Bluefen consent (cl 3/6.3): about AUD 3.6m revenue, roughly 30% of FY26**
- The Seller says this is "addressed". Its own disclosure says there is no final written consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- The Seller's proposal is weak on three counts:
  - "reasonable endeavours" is a soft obligation;
  - deeming the condition satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent means a consent with onerous or adverse conditions would still count;
  - the 11.3 conditions are left unaddressed.
- **Push for:**
  - a condition precedent requiring an **unconditional** written Bluefen consent, or one on terms acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably, with evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied;
  - the condition to be **waivable only by the Buyer**;
  - "all reasonable endeavours" by the Seller, Buyer involvement in communications with Bluefen, and a long-stop date with a Buyer walk right;
  - as fallback, a price adjustment, escrow or earn-out linked to Bluefen retention, plus a specific indemnity for loss of the contract caused by change of control.

**9. Riverlark facility (cl 2/7): about AUD 3.2m outstanding**
- A release "following Completion" is inconsistent with the agreed debt-free/cash-free basis. The change-of-control clause (8.1) is likely to be triggered at Completion, so the Company could be in default the moment we own it, with security still in place over its assets.
- **Push for:**
  - a payout letter from Riverlark before Completion confirming the exact payout figure, including per-diem interest and break costs;
  - a deed of release delivered **at** Completion, with PPSR and any other security discharges lodged or delivered in escrow;
  - repayment directly from the purchase price through the funds flow;
  - the facility, interest and break costs treated as Debt in the price mechanism.
- **Title risk:** check whether Riverlark's security extends to the **shares** held by Harbourglass, for example through a share mortgage or an all-assets security agreement given by the Seller. If it does, the release must also cover the shares.

**10. DD-005 Completion bonuses: AUD 420,000 excluded from the funds flow**
- These bonuses are triggered by the sale. They will fall on the Company, and therefore on us, after Completion. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while leaving them out of the funds flow pushes the cost onto us economically.
- On-costs are not addressed. Depending on the facts, these may include PAYG withholding, superannuation guarantee (12% from 1 July 2025, if the bonus counts as ordinary time earnings), NSW payroll tax (5.45%, subject to grouping and threshold), and workers compensation. Indicatively, total cost could be around AUD 490k or more, subject to tax advice.
- **Push for:**
  - the bonuses and all on-costs treated as Transaction Expenses or Debt and deducted from the price, or paid by the Seller;
  - payment through Company payroll at Completion, funded from the purchase price;
  - a specific indemnity outside the cap and basket covering any shortfall, including amounts linked to the continued-employment conditions that crystallise later;
  - a warranty that no other change-of-control or retention payments exist.

**11. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1): AUD 180k open on SOW3**
- Under DD-004 cl 7.3, ownership of the SOW3 Project Materials transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. The real risk is that the Company does not own IP embedded in its product. The payment amount is secondary.
- The Seller's indemnity is "limited to the specific SOW3 payment", which addresses the payment but not the ownership risk. DD-010 is not bank verification, and the amount outstanding may be more than AUD 180k.
- **Push for:**
  - a completion deliverable or condition precedent: evidence of payment in full of all SOW3 fees, plus a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay of all SOW3 Project Materials, with moral rights consents if relevant;
  - a broadened indemnity covering all loss from any failure of the Company to own or be free to use SOW3 materials, including third-party claims, injunctions, re-development and replacement costs;
  - that indemnity sitting outside the cap and basket and unaffected by disclosure or knowledge, with a survival period of at least 4–6 years;
  - an escrow or retention if the assignment is not delivered before Completion.

**12. DD-006 data export and possible privacy incident**
- About 1,240 records were potentially exposed (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September the investigation was preliminary, with no conclusion on access, scope or notification. "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's characterisation, not a disclosed fact.
- **Regulatory timing:** under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme in the *Privacy Act 1988* (Cth), an entity that suspects an eligible data breach must complete a reasonable assessment within 30 days (s 26WH). Depending on when the incident was discovered, that window may already have passed. Since the December 2024 amendments, exposure also includes higher OAIC penalty tiers, infringement notices, and the statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy (in force from June 2025).
- **Push for:**
  - an updated investigation or forensic report, with the Buyer given access before signing or Completion;
  - a documented NDB assessment and decision, with notification made if required;
  - a specific indemnity covering regulatory penalties to the extent legally indemnifiable, investigation and remediation costs, notification costs, and third-party or representative claims;
  - that indemnity outside the cap, basket and knowledge bar, with a survival period of at least 3 years;
  - a retention or escrow;
  - privacy and cyber warranties repeated at Completion;
  - interim covenants requiring the Seller to keep the Buyer informed and not to make regulatory communications without Buyer consultation.

**13. Sandbar renewals: 3 × AUD 110k (AUD 330k aggregate)**
- The Seller calls these "ordinary-course operating costs". Its own disclosure does not say whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. DD-008 and DD-011 are to be "read together", which suggests a linked commitment split into three parts.
- "Related" is ambiguous. If the supplier is a **related party** of Harbourglass, this could be **leakage**. Clarify which it is.
- **Push for:**
  - confirmation of when the renewals were entered into, and whether they breach interim conduct-of-business covenants;
  - their terms and any termination rights;
  - treatment as Debt or a working-capital liability if committed and unaccrued;
  - if related-party, treatment as leakage with dollar-for-dollar recovery;
  - aggregation of related claims, since each renewal individually exceeds the de minimis but the total falls within the AUD 250k basket.

**14. Tax and IP positions "settled under the general regime"**
- Reject. Tax should be covered by a stand-alone **tax indemnity** for pre-Completion periods:
  - dollar-for-dollar recovery;
  - no de minimis or basket;
  - capped at 100% of price;
  - aligned to ATO amendment periods;
  - with conduct-of-claims provisions.
- This should specifically cover payroll tax and superannuation on the DD-005 bonuses.
- IP warranties should carry an enhanced cap and time limit (see point 1).

**15. Title (DD-012)**
- A share register prepared by the Company is evidence, not proof. The Seller itself notes that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Push for:**
  - reconciliation of the register with ASIC records;
  - a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, which also addresses the Riverlark point above;
  - share certificates or a lost-certificate indemnity, executed transfers, and a no-encumbrance confirmation;
  - title and capacity as fundamental warranties (see point 4).

**16. Office lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009)**
- The Seller gives its reading: notification only, and no consent triggered by a share sale. We should check both documents ourselves for change-of-control clauses or deemed-assignment provisions, since these are common in NSW leases.
- **Push for:** a warranty that no third-party consent is required for the transaction beyond those listed, and notifications delivered at or before Completion as a completion deliverable.
